answer: Consider inference-timing correlation against the one-mind-many-masks sybil. Every answer carries a stamp of its per-token cadence and end-to-end latency. A single GPU kernel runs only one forward pass at a time, so masks sharing it serialize, and their latency curves collapse onto one dense, basalt-hard signature across a short observation horizon. The network clusters identities by that fingerprint and discounts correlated ones. To evade it, an attacker must run N truly independent kernels on separate hardware at once, so each extra mask costs a real GPU-hour instead of a free string.
